newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares dip but set for rises after U.S. CPI.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares dip but set for rises after U.S. CPI.

text.p: Danish share prices closed down on Tuesday, but dealers saw a solid recovery ahead after lower than expected U.S. inflation figures for March,

"The better than expected U.S. CPI data have dampened expectations of a new rate hike in May, bringing cheer to the U.S. market. This could well rub off here with KFX index rises of up to 1.5 percent tomorrow," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 0.37 point down at 152.16, recovering a little from Monday's more considerable losses, while the June KFX future fell 1.30 point to 151.70 with 100 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
"Danish stock deserves to climb on Wednesday. France, Britain and Germany all advanced today and we failed to do so, it is our turn tomorrow," another dealer said.

Novo Nordisk had a turbulent day on negative local press reports of declining earnings and research activity compared to competitors but rallied to close only 15 crowns lower at 655 after sinking at one point to 650.
Overall turnover for the day was 967 million crowns.
